newsitem.title: ANGOLA: BHP SEES LONG TERM INTEREST IN ANGOLA.
newsitem.headline: BHP SEES LONG TERM INTEREST IN ANGOLA.

text.p: Australian mining giant Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), recently offered the right to operate one of Angola's offshore oil blocks, has a long-term interest in the country's deep water, a BHP official said on Tuesday.
"Our ambitions in Angola certainly go beyond the current bid round," chief executive officer for BHP's subsidiary, BHP Petroleum, John O'Connor told Reuters in an interview.
Though BHP was recently offered the operatorship of Block 21, O'Connor stressed the deal was not yet final.
"This deal is still subject to ultimate approval by the government," he said.
If the deal is approved, as is widely expected by oil analysts, it would be the first operatorship awarded to BHP and the first to an Australian company in Angola.
O'Connor, who was on a visit to Angola, said BHP saw the future of oil production in the country's deep-water blocs.
"We have demonstrated a track record in deep water," he said.
"We recently did a well in the Gulf of Mexico at 2,000 metres. There are only a handful of companies in the world that can go that deep, and the future of oil in Angola is at those kind of depths."
BHP is also engaged in the mining sector and O'Connor said the company would explore possibilities of looking into mining in Angola.
The country, although known mostly for its diamond production, also has significant gold reserves, according to local analysts.
"I would expect our mining colleagues to take a look at opportunities here," O'Connor said.
"We certainly bring more to Angola than oil and gas expertise. There is a great potential for other investments here as well," he added.
BHP was a minority shareholder in Block 4 with Canada's Ranger Oil Ltd , but has now withdrawn.
The company's only other involvement in oil in West Africa is as a participant in three offshore blocks in Gabon, O'Connor said.
